findings.problem: loads_json converts UnicodeDecodeError and JSONDecodeError to ValueError but not RecursionError. A snapshot within the 8 MiB limit consisting of deeply nested arrays (e.g. 100k '[') escapes as RecursionError instead of a clean validation rejection.
findings.fix: Catch RecursionError alongside UnicodeDecodeError in loads_json and re-raise ValueError('JSON nesting too deep'), or pre-reject raw inputs whose bracket depth exceeds a small constant.

findings.problem: _text only rejects C0 controls (<32). DEL (0x7f), C1 controls (0x80-0x9f), bidi overrides, and zero-width characters pass, and leading/trailing whitespace is preserved. So reviewer_id 'x' vs 'x ' or 'x\u200b' count as 'distinct reviewers', and reason text may carry invisible/bidi characters into the report.
findings.reproduction: compare_readings(m, sha, a, b) with a['reviewer_id']='claude', b['reviewer_id']='claude ' succeeds
findings.fix: Reject chars where unicodedata.category(c) in {'Cc','Cf','Cs','Co','Cn'} except \n\t, and compare reviewer_id after .strip() (or require value == value.strip()).

findings.problem: Artifact name is derived from pitch_key with only ':' replaced. If validate_input does not restrict pitch_key to a filesystem-safe charset with uniqueness after ':'->'_' mapping, two frames can map to the same name and exports[name] silently overwrites the first SVG; artifacts list and comparison.json then omit a frame with no error. Separately, keys containing '/', '\\', '..', NUL, or Windows reserved stems (CON, NUL, COM1) would escape or fail at write time. Conditional on core validation not shown.
findings.reproduction: Manifest with pitch_keys 'g1:p1' and 'g1_p1' (if core accepts both) -> one SVG written, counts/report list two frames.
findings.fix: Before assignment: if name in exports: raise ValueError('duplicate artifact name'). Also assert pitch_key matches ^[A-Za-z0-9:_-]+$ locally (or document that core enforces it) so the write path cannot contain separators or reserved names.

findings.problem: _is_link falls back to False for junctions on Python < 3.12 (no Path.is_junction). Containment is still enforced by the resolve().relative_to checks on both image and destination, so this only weakens the stated 'no junction' policy, not containment.
findings.reproduction: Py3.11 on Windows: junction inside source dir pointing inside source dir is accepted.
findings.fix: Document minimum Python 3.12, or compare path.resolve() to path.absolute() per component as a fallback.

findings.problem: exports and base64 rasters for all frames are held in memory before writing; worst case ~43 MiB per frame SVG plus decoded pixels up to the PIL bomb threshold (~350 MB RGBA). Acceptable for a local 3-frame tool; noted only because the 32 MiB cap does not bound decoded size.
findings.fix: Optional: lower Image.MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS to the manifest-declared width*height before open, which also rejects dimension mismatch earlier.

findings.problem: main catches ValueError/OSError only. KeyError from by_key lookup or a frame missing from report['frames'] would print a traceback. Not reachable if compare_readings enforces one-to-one frame identity as stated.
findings.fix: No change required; optionally catch KeyError with a 'report/manifest frame mismatch' message.

findings.assessment: Catching RecursionError inside loads_json and re-raising ValueError('JSON nesting too deep') from exc converts the crash into the same bounded validation-failure class as the other JSON errors. CPython's C scanner (and the pure-Python fallback) both raise RecursionError for deep arrays, so the except clause is reached. The regression test is sound: 100_000-deep nesting far exceeds any default recursion limit, the anchored match pins the exact message, and the __cause__ assertion proves the chained path rather than an incidental ValueError. Assumptions: json.loads is inside the same try block as the UnicodeDecodeError handler (the diff shows it adjacent, consistent with that), and any pre-parse byte-size cap is above ~200 KB so the test input actually reaches the parser. The claimed passing run was not reproduced here.

The conditional finding assumed pitch_key could contain '_' or arbitrary text. _identity enforces fullmatch of [1-9][0-9]{0,10}:[1-9][0-9]{0,5}:[1-9][0-9]{0,5}: digits and exactly two colons only, no underscore, no path separators, no case-variant characters, and the first segment is pinned to game_pk. On that domain the mapping ':' -> '_' is injective: the output has exactly two underscores at the colon positions and digits elsewhere, so distinct inputs cannot collide and 'g1:p1'/'g1_p1' are both rejected at validation. validate_input additionally rejects duplicate pitch_key strings per manifest, and image names are deduplicated casefolded. Digits-only output also removes Windows case-insensitive and reserved-name concerns. Condition for closure: export only consumes frames that passed validate_input (or output derived from them). If export can be fed an unvalidated manifest, the finding reopens; stated as an assumption, not verified here.
Metadata whitespace was never a model-identity control; identity is bound to the CLI receipt. Accepted as documented behaviour, not a defect.

No runtime junction ban is claimed for Python <3.12; the strict policy now requires 3.12. Acceptable provided the existing containment check still executes on all versions and the 3.12 requirement is stated where operators will see it. A sys.version_info guard would make this enforced rather than documented; optional, not blocking.
Holding three small PNGs in memory is bounded by the 32768x32768 and frame-count caps already validated; acceptable.
